newsitem.title: CHINA: Six month wait for decision on Kai Tak cargo facility.
newsitem.headline: Six month wait for decision on Kai Tak cargo facility.

text.p: Freight forwarders in Hong Kong face at least another six months of uncertainty before they can plan their business strategy for the opening of the Chek Lap Kok(CLK) airport due to open next April, air cargo sources said.

Fearing high transport costs and user charges at Hong Kong's new airport, many small and medium-sized forwarding firms hope they can retain their existing warehousing facilities near Kai Tak airport, the sources told Reuters on Wednesday.
They want the airport's highly automated cargo Terminal 2 operated by Hong Kong Air Cargo Terminals Limited (HACTL), to remain open as a consolidation centre.
Cargo could then be transported along a new motorway network which links CLK with Kowloon.
The 261-member Hong Kong Association of Freight Forwarding Agents Ltd (HAFFA) and HACTL have made a joint appeal to the government to save Terminal 2 from closure, the sources added.

Property analysts consider the Kai Tak airport site to be prime real estate which would earn the government a huge cash windfall when redeveloped. The removal of height restrictions on buildings now on Kai Tak's flight path could also prove lucrative for developers.

A Hong Kong Planning, Environment and Lands Bureau spokeswoman told Reuters that freight forwarders will have to wait at least another six months before a decision is announced as the government is awaiting the end of a three year study into the future of south east Kowloon and the Kai Tak area.
"It should be completed by the end of the year or early next year," she said.
That would give freight forwarders just a few months to decide what to do and frustration is rising, the air cargo sources said.
HAFFA chairman Anthony Lau, also chairman and chief executive of freight forwarding firm Baltrans Holdings Ltd said he was disappointed by the new delay.

"Many small and medium size firms would not have to increase their costs if Terminal 2 is retained and their whole operation would be simplified. Not knowing if they can stay where they are or whether they must move closer to the new airport mean months more of uncertainty for many firms. It is a pity because they wanted a quick reply," Lau said.
